package_info.why_malicious: These packages masquerade as legitimate or useful tools (e.g., TikTok filter removers) but contain obfuscated code that downloads and executes WASP stealer malware, exfiltrating sensitive user data. The packages use deceptive tactics such as copying legitimate project metadata and StarJacking to appear trustworthy.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code decodes a base64-encoded payload and executes it, which downloads and runs WASP stealer malware, exfiltrating sensitive data to attacker-controlled servers.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated, base64-encoded code executed at import-time is a classic malware technique to evade detection and run arbitrary payloads.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not execute arbitrary code on import, especially not code that is obfuscated and network-active.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Base64 decoding and dynamic execution may be used in some advanced legitimate tools for plugin loading, but never in this context.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During requirements installation, the code executes a base64-encoded payload, which downloads and runs WASP stealer malware, exfiltrating sensitive data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: requirements.txt should only list dependencies, not contain executable code. Executable code in requirements.txt is a clear sign of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: requirements.txt is not expected to contain or execute code, only package names.

attack_chain.action: User is lured via TikTok/Discord to download and install the malicious package or clone the GitHub repo.
User installs the package or runs the provided .bat/script, triggering requirements.txt or import-time execution.
Obfuscated Python code is executed, which downloads and runs WASP stealer malware.
WASP stealer exfiltrates sensitive data (credentials, tokens, files) to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated base64-encoded code executed at import-time or during installation
Unexpected network connections to known C2 or Discord webhook endpoints
file_indicators: requirements.txt with Python code instead of package names
models.py or other core files with obfuscated one-liners
Presence of packages named pyshftuler, pyiopcs, tiktok-filter-api, pydesings, pyshdesings
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan for base64-encoded or obfuscated code in package files, especially in models.py or requirements.txt. Flag any requirements.txt that contains executable code. Monitor for network connections to known C2 domains and Discord webhooks. Alert on dynamic code execution patterns (exec/compile) in third-party packages.
